tower-of-hanoi.title: Move largest disk first if not on target
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the largest disk that still needs to be placed is not already on its goal peg, move it before handling any smaller disks. Doing so prevents later dead‑ends where the largest disk becomes blocked by smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the current configuration has the largest needed disk on a peg different from its goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to shuffle several small disks while the largest needed disk remains on a non‑goal peg, leading to extra or illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve subproblem after moving largest disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After the largest needed disk has been placed on its target peg, treat the remaining n‑1 disks as a fresh Tower of Hanoi problem, ignoring the already‑settled disk. This isolates the sub‑task and guarantees correctness.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after the largest needed disk has been moved to its goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move other disks without resetting the subproblem, which leaves some disks on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive move sequence for k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To transfer a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the target. This pattern respects the size rule at every step.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a contiguous stack of k disks between two pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk before the k‑1 smaller disks have been relocated, which violates the rule that a larger disk cannot sit on a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as final parseable output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer must end with the complete move list in bracket notation; any text after it will be ignored by the verifier. The parser extracts the last bracketed list it sees.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer to the problem.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory sentences after the move list, causing the parser to miss the moves entirely.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure the resulting configuration matches the goal exactly. This catches missing or mis‑ordered moves before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before submitting the final move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because the final state was not double‑checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Concise final move list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Provide only the move list as the final output, without extra explanations, duplicate lists, or formatting that could confuse the parser. A clean, solitary list guarantees the verifier reads the intended moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a second copy of the move list after the first, which leads the parser to read an empty or wrong list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, confirm that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger. This prevents illegal placements that the verifier will reject.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 while disk 1 sits on top of it, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere. This ensures the size rule is never violated when the larger disk arrives.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to move a larger disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 onto a peg that already contains disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving blocking smaller disks onto the target peg of a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto the destination peg of a larger disk that still needs to be moved there, because the small disk will block the larger one. Keep the target peg clear of any non‑final small disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to move a small disk that is not yet at its final location.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto the goal peg before disk 3 has been placed there, making it impossible to later move disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear source peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you intend to move is not the topmost on its source peg because a smaller disk sits on it, first move that smaller disk to another peg (using the smallest disk as a temporary buffer if needed) before moving the larger disk. This guarantees the larger disk can be lifted legally.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the source peg of a larger disk has a smaller disk on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 3 while disk 1 remains on the same peg, without first relocating disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to output the moves or assume the answer is implicit.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a non‑empty list of moves as the final output.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops generation early, leaving the move list unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the full sequence before writing and ensure the answer ends with the complete list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the goal without checking the current stack order on the source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is the top disk on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a smaller disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model treats any legal move as acceptable and does not anticipate that the small disk will block larger disks that must later occupy the same peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: When a small disk is not yet at its final position, avoid placing it on the goal peg until all larger disks that belong there have been moved.
